b: We talk a lot about both gratitude and check-ins on this blog, and for good reason – both are beneficial habits to establish in your marriage. This 5-minute check-in framework is the perfect way to combine them. Let’s dive in.
Three simple questions are all you need. The goal is to keep it short and uplifting – a warm moment of connection versus a heavy discussion.

What’s something small you’ve noticed that you’re grateful for?
Learning to see and appreciate the little things is one part of the equation; the other is expressing this appreciation to your spouse. Maybe it’s how they always make your coffee in the morning, or that they handled a tough parenting situation really well. It’s easy for these small moments to get lost in the day-to-day shuffle. Taking the time to truly acknowledge them helps prevent you from taking each other for granted.

What’s something that’s been hard – but you’re still grateful for?
Feeling grateful doesn’t mean everything is easy. Whether it’s an exhausting new phase of parenting, a stressful period at work, or working through an ongoing conflict together, gratitude often goes hand in hand with adversity. Leaving space for both helps you see how resilient you can be and the ways in which you and your marriage have grown.

What do you appreciate about each other that you haven’t said in a while?
Think of something specific about your spouse – it could be a quality, something they did, or a unique thing you truly love about them. Maybe you haven’t commented on it lately because it seems so innate or just part of who they are. That’s all the more reason to make a point to do it. Over time, you might lose sight of the amazing things your spouse brings to your marriage, and they may not be aware of it themselves. Saying it out loud is a great reminder for both of you.
This check-in doesn’t have to be limited to Thanksgiving Day. Here are a few ways you can sprinkle it into your marriage – do what works for you!

Make it a tradition
It pretty much goes without saying that gratitude is in the air this time of year. Start a new annual tradition by doing the check-in every week of November, in the week leading up to Thanksgiving, or some similarly seasonal variation. Chances are you’re already thinking about what you’’re thankful for – this gives you a dedicated time and concrete way to express it. Consider jotting down your answers so you can look back on each year.

Incorporate it throughout the year
Gratitude isn’t only important in November. Cultivate a grateful mindset year-round by penciling in this check-in once a month, or even on a weekly basis if that floats your boat. Already have a regular marriage check-in? Great! This is a simple way to end it on a positive note.

Tie it to other occasions
Whether it’s your anniversary, your birthday, or every date night, there are many other opportunities to make a gratitude check-in a regular thing. Similar to making it a seasonal tradition, it can quickly become a meaningful chance to reflect on where you are now and your journey since you last checked in.

When a challenging season is taking its toll
When life gets crazy, it’s easy to fall into a negative mindset. You start taking it out on each other, and your connection suffers. A gratitude check-in can help reset your perspective when things have gotten clouded by stress or adversity.

This time of year can be a lot. The obligations, expectations, and emotions on top of the sheer busyness of the season can leave you both feeling drained. This gratitude check-in is a great way to pause, recenter yourselves, and say thank you – whether it’s the week of Thanksgiving or throughout the whole year.
